checks.issue: THE CHANT ENDS WITH NO FULL STOP. Every other couplet in it closes with one — verses 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and 28 all do — but อายานัญจาภิวุฑฒิยา simply stops, with clear white paper after it, checked at 2x on an isolated crop. Reproduced without. The next chant's title follows after a gap, so this really is the last line of the chant and not a page-turn effect.

A MID-WORD TWO-COLUMN JOIN, the same thing page 67 verse 10 did. The left cell ends ธะรันโต โพธิยา สักขิ- WITH A HYPHEN and the right cell begins ภูตานันตะคุเณนะ, so the halves join with NO space: สักขิภูตานันตะคุเณนะ. Verse 26 does it again — ปัจฉิมาชะนะตาภูตะ- joining สัตตานุกัมปะมานะสา — and both are rejoined with the hyphen dropped. That is three such joins in this chant, which is strong confirmation the rows read across and not down.

THE SAME WORD IS PRINTED TWO WAYS TWO PAGES APART. Here it is ปะฏิคคัณหาตุ with NO mark over the ณ; on page 67 verse 59 the book prints ปะฏิคคัณ์หาตุ WITH the small conjunct mark. Both read at magnification and both entered as their own page prints them. This is the same class as page 60's อุณหัสสะ, where the printer omitted a mark standard editions carry — worth knowing that this book is inconsistent with itself about the mark, not only about which mark it is.

กะโรนาตา is unusual — standard Pali would give karontā, กะโรนตา, for the present participle. The page appears to print an extra า after the น. Reproduced as read and transliterated to match. Not confident; worth one look.

เอกัตตะ stands without a case ending where the sense wants 'in one place' — standard would be ekattha or ekatthaṃ. Reproduced exactly as printed rather than completed, and the English follows the sense rather than the form.

NO COLOPHON on this chant either. It ends at verse 30 and the next title follows, with no centred นิฏฐิตา line. The ‼ CONTINUES marker page 67 left on it must now be removed, since the chant is complete across pages 67 and 68.

checks.issue: THE PAGE ENDS MID-UNIT. The last printed line stops at สะเทวะเก โลเก สะมาระเก with no comma, and the parallel passage on page 66 continues สะพ์รัห์มะเก, — so this unit is incomplete and is recorded with […] rather than finished from the earlier page or from memory. Page 69 completes it, and must carry the SAME verse number 9 with the whole line.

THIS PAGE PUNCTUATES DIFFERENTLY FROM ITS TWIN, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS NOW CONFIRMED FROM BOTH SIDES. Page 66's Visākha offering prints มัชฌิเมสุ, and ชะนะปะเทสุ, with a comma after EACH, giving two one-word units. Page 68 prints มัชฌิเมสุ ชะนะปะเทสุ, with NO comma between them — line 2 ends มัชฌิเมสุ with clear space and no mark, read at 2.3x. So the same sentence is pointed two ways in two parallel chants, and this entry has one unit where page 66 has two. Both entered as their own page prints them. This was raised as a doubt on page 66 and is now evidence rather than a doubt; one look settles which pointing the printer intended.

Page 66's twin prints ขัตติโย ชาติยา โคตะโม โคตเตนะ, as one unit and so does this page, but page 64's long invitation splits the same words differently again. The three printings of this opening are worth reading side by side once, because they are close enough that a difference reads as a mistake rather than as the book.

SECOND OF THE FOUR PARALLEL OFFERINGS. Visākha is at 66, this at 68, Māgha at 71 and Āsāḷha at 75, all under the same title but for the day. It must NOT be stubbed as a repeat of page 66's: it is separately printed, separately titled, and already differs in its punctuation at verse 5.
The title is THAI, not Pali, so title_pali is empty and title_roman carries the romanisation the book's own contents already prints for this line, rather than a fresh one.

The Saraphañña verses that began on page 67 are finished here, so stage 2 must REMOVE their ‼ CONTINUES marker; the new Aṭṭhamī offering then opens its own, since page 69 carries the rest of it. Four things worth reading. (1) The Saraphañña verses end with NO full stop where every other couplet in them has one — checked on an isolated crop with clear paper after it, and reproduced without. (2) Verses 24 and 26 join MID-WORD across the gutter, the left cell ending in a hyphen, exactly as page 67 verse 10 did; three such joins in one chant is strong confirmation these rows read across and not down. (3) ปะฏิคคัณหาตุ is printed here WITHOUT the small mark where page 67 prints ปะฏิคคัณ์หาตุ WITH it — the same word, two pages apart, two ways. That is the book being inconsistent about whether the mark is there at all, which is a different question from which of the two marks it is. (4) The new offering's verse 5 CONFIRMS a doubt raised on page 66: the twin passages are pointed differently, page 66 putting a comma after มัชฌิเมสุ where this page does not.
